note: Draft 1.1, 'The Lakh' (the user's yes at the story gate, 18 Nov). One voice, af_heart at pace 1.0 (takes 2 and 3 at 0.96 and 1.04): Meta's dub handles one speaker. Worded for the ear before the first run: 'can't leave barefoot' is 'And no groom leaves barefoot' (a weak nt is one sound from its opposite, 38); 'Five of them' is 'five sisters' (the cold reader could take 'five of them' for five of the rounds); 'You didn't save him a rupee' has an alternative with no contraction (n21b) for the checks to judge. Indian words planned by hand (memory indian-word-pronunciation), three plans each for joota chupai and mehendi, two for lakh (n08b, n20b): the phoneme ear and the user's ear pick. The t's of thirty, twenty and seventy are planned as real t's (the voice flaps them otherwise).

say.mehendi: m ɛ h ə n d iː

lines.text: You're guarding the groom's shoes.
Because at many North Indian weddings, the bride's sisters steal them, and he pays to get them back.
It's called joota chupai.
It's called joota chupai.
It's called joota chupai.
Seven rounds of the fire, five sisters, and a trick every round.
So which one gets his shoes? Pick a number.
Then number five hands you a baby, and nobody says no to a baby.
When you look up, number four's gone, and so are his shoes.
And now they want one lakh.
And now they want one lakh.
You laugh.
They walk off.
And no groom leaves barefoot.
So they come down. Fifty-one thousand.
Thirty-one.
Twenty-one.
That's seventy-nine thousand off.
You'd take that, wouldn't you?
He does.
Then they show you their hands.
It's in their mehendi, from last night: twenty-one thousand.
